messages.content: What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?

message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is normally **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
Because the two cities switch daylight‑saving time at slightly different dates, the gap can briefly be **8 hours**:

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Standard time (both on winter time) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | 9 h |
| After LA switches to DST but before Berlin does (late March) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | 8 h |
| After Berlin switches to DST but before LA does (late October) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | 8 h |
| Both on DST | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | 9 h |

So, for most of the year Berlin is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles, but during the brief overlap periods around the DST transition dates the difference is 8 hours.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?" They want the time difference. We need to consider daylight saving changes. Los Angeles is in Pacific Time (PT), which is UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 DST. Berlin is Central European Time (CET) UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 DST. So difference: Standard: Berlin is 9 hours ahead of LA. During DST: LA is UTC-7, Berlin UTC+2, difference 9 hours. Wait: Let's compute: If both are on DST: LA UTC-7, Berlin UTC+2, difference 9 hours. If LA on DST but Berlin not? That can't happen because they shift at same time? Actually DST start times differ: Berlin starts last Sunday of March, LA starts second Sunday of March. So there can be a period where Berlin is still CET (UTC+1) while LA is PDT (UTC-7). That would be 8 hours difference. Similarly, when Berlin is on DST but LA hasn't yet? That occurs after Berlin DST start but before LA DST start? Actually Berlin DST starts last Sunday of March, LA DST starts second Sunday of March. So after second Sunday of March, LA is on DST, Berlin still on standard until last Sunday. So difference 8 hours. After last Sunday, both on DST, difference 9 hours. Then after LA ends DST (first Sunday of November), Berlin still DST until last Sunday of October? Actually Berlin DST ends last Sunday of October, LA ends first Sunday of November. So after Berlin ends DST but LA still DST? That period: Berlin UTC+1, LA UTC-7, difference 8 hours. After LA ends DST, Berlin still DST until last Sunday of October? Wait timeline: In fall, Berlin ends DST last Sunday of October, LA ends DST first Sunday of November. So after Berlin ends DST but before LA ends DST, Berlin UTC+1, LA UTC-7, difference 8 hours. After LA ends DST, Berlin still DST until last Sunday of October? Actually Berlin ended DST earlier, so after Berlin ends DST, Berlin UTC+1, LA UTC-8, difference 9 hours. So difference can be 8 or 9 hours depending on DST overlap.

Thus answer: Usually 9 hours ahead, but during DST transitions it can be 8 hours. Provide explanation. No function call needed.
